title: Strategic Account Executive Enterprise - DACH
description:
🪐 Discover our galaxy 

Join the Future of Work ! Malt is Europe's leading freelance marketplace, connecting over 1,000,000 talented freelancers with 100,000+ companies. Founded in 2013, we're transforming how work gets done through our tech-powered, human-centered platform. What makes us different: 

- A diverse team of 600 Malters across 6 European countries 

- A culture that champions equality (50% of our Comex are women) and inclusive growth 

- Backed by top investors including ISAI, Serena Capital, Eurazeo Growth, Goldman Sachs, and BPI 

- A mission to give everyone the freedom to work differently 

Ready to help shape the future of work? Your next chapter starts here! 

At Malt we believe that Ambition is the Way, so all lists of missions and responsibilities are non-exhaustive. 

The Mission 🪐 

- The Situation: Malt is cementing its position as the undeniable leader in the European freelance economy. While our tech-powered platform connects over 1,000,000 top-tier freelancers with 100,000+ companies, the DACH Enterprise sector presents a massive, untapped frontier. This market is dominated by complex, multinational corporate structures with deeply entrenched procurement protocols that are ripe for disruption.

- The Task: We are not hiring you to manage an existing portfolio or farm warm leads. You are being brought in to architect and own the zero-to-one enterprise acquisition strategy for the DACH region. Operating as the "founder" of your territory, your mandate is to systematically penetrate massive global accounts, navigate labyrinthine procurement structures, and secure highly scalable, multi-country Master Service Agreements (MSAs) that will cement Malt's dominance in the German-speaking market and beyond.

Key Responsibilities ✨ 

Pillar 1: Strategic Territory Architecture & Hunting 

- Action: Map out complex, global enterprise accounts within the DACH region, aggressively designing and executing surgical prospecting strategies to breach heavily fortified multi-stakeholder environments (Procurement, HR, and independent Business Units).

- Output: A localized, highly qualified pipeline of net-new DACH Enterprise logos and concrete, multi-threaded stakeholder maps.

- Metrics of Performance: Enterprise GSV Pipeline Generated and CRM forecast integrity.

Pillar 2: Deal Orchestration & RFP Command 

- Action: Run rigorous, in-depth discovery utilizing the full MEDDIC framework to validate severe business pain, identify the true Economic Buyer, and aggressively lead end-to-end RFI/RFP processes alongside our Bid Management and technical teams.

- Output: Compelling, ROI-driven business proposals and precisely engineered enterprise pilot programs designed to prove undeniable platform value.

- Metrics of Performance: RFI/RFP Win Rate and Pilot-to-MSA Conversion Rate.

Pillar 3: Heavy-Weight Negotiation & Scalable Revenue Activation 

- Action: Command ruthless, complex negotiations for global Master Service Agreements involving tight friction with Legal, Finance, and Procurement across multiple countries. Upon signature, engineer the scalable handover strategy to the local Account Management teams.

- Output: Executed, multi-country MSAs and comprehensive post-signature deployment kickoff plans.

- Metrics of Performance: Total Contract Value (TCV) Signed and Deal Velocity (managing complex cycles efficiently without losing momentum).

Requirements & The Skills Matrix 🔍 
Proven Mastery (What you have already built): 

- A minimum of 8 years of quantifiable, proven track record hunting and closing complex, 7-figure B2B sales cycles within a SaaS/Tech environment.

- Deep familiarity with the staffing, "future of work" industry, MSPs, or Tier 1 recruitment groups.

- Demonstrated success navigating extremely long sales cycles and managing strategic concessions to close highly scalable deals.

- Native-level fluency in German and full professional fluency in English.

Skills You Will Deploy & Develop: 

- Advanced MEDDIC Mastery: You will deploy this framework with such rigor that you act as the internal benchmark and can actively coach others on its nuances.

- C-Suite ROI Narrative Construction: Mastering the art of delivering disruptive narratives that challenge legacy customer assumptions and shift C-level perspectives on the "Future of Work."

- Cross-Border Deal Structuring: Developing top-tier acumen in multi-country legal, financial, and compliance orchestration.

The Self-Selection Filter ❓ 

This role is perfect for you if: 

- You are an elite hunter who actively enjoys the strategic friction of a complex enterprise sales cycle and navigating massive corporate red tape.

- You operate with extreme ownership—you treat your pipeline like your own startup's P&L and do not wait for permission or inbound leads to execute.

- You naturally think in terms of "Economic Buyers," "Decision Criteria," and "Validation Events" rather than just "having good meetings."

This role is NOT for you if: 

- You rely heavily on inbound marketing or a pre-packaged SDR playbook to hit your pipeline numbers.

- You get easily intimidated by heavy-weight legal negotiations, aggressive procurement teams, or highly structured RFP processes.

- You prefer predictable, transactional account maintenance over the high-stakes thrill of net-new, multi-country enterprise acquisition.

30-60-90 Day Impact Plan 🏁 

- Day 30: Submerge into our marketplace mechanics, master the Malt value proposition, and map the top tier of DACH global enterprise accounts. Output: Delivery of your fully architected account penetration strategy.

- Day 60: Execute initial outreach, identify key Economic Buyers within target accounts, and begin orchestrating your first high-stakes pilot phases. Output: Establish a predictable, MEDDIC-qualified enterprise pipeline.

- Day 90: Take absolute control of your Metrics of Performance . Lead your first complex RFI/RFP processes or MSA negotiations end-to-end and initiate scalable handover plans. Output: Secure early enterprise traction that directly impacts the regional bottom line.

How to join the mission? 🚀 

- First Call (45m): High-level alignment with Niko (Talent Acquisition Lead) to audit your background and entrepreneurial drive.

title: Talent Acquisition Intern
description:
Talent Acquisition Intern

Deine Mission bei trawa

Bei trawa sind wir überzeugt: Die Energiewende beginnt bei den Menschen, die sie möglich machen. Du willst leistungsstarke Teams mit aufbauen und Recruiting von Grund auf so lernen, dass es wirklich Wirkung hat? Dann bist du bei trawa genau richtig.

Als Talent Acquisition Intern bist du das operative Rückgrat unseres Talent-Teams und sorgst mit uns dafür, dass die richtigen Menschen zu trawa finden. Du hältst unsere Prozesse am Laufen, gestaltest reibungslose Candidate Journeys, räumst administrative Hürden aus dem Weg und hilfst, ein Hiring-Erlebnis zu bauen, das hängen bleibt. So bringst du direkt mit voran, was uns antreibt: Unternehmen den Zugang zu echter, grüner Energie zu ermöglichen.

Diese Rolle passt perfekt zu dir, wenn du Talent Acquisition hands-on lernen willst, gerne mit modernen Tools und KI-Lösungen arbeitest und direkt sehen möchtest, wie dein Beitrag das gesamte Team schneller und besser macht.

Bei uns findest du keine starren Strukturen - dafür Gestaltungsspielraum, Vertrauen und ein Team, das die Energiewende gemeinsam voranbringt.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

Was du bei uns vorantreibst

- Bewerbungen screenen : Bewerbungen entlang klarer Basic Requirements checken und Kandidat:innen schnell und fair durch die Pipeline steuern.

- ATS & Tracking : Unser ATS sauber, aktuell und strukturiert halten - plus einfache Tracker pflegen, damit alle jederzeit den Status im Blick haben

- Interview-Organisation : Interviews end-to-end organisieren: Termine finden, Kalender koordinieren und das Team mit allen Infos versorgen.

- Candidate Communication : Eine starke Candidate Experience sicherstellen - zeitnahe Updates geben, Fragen beantworten und durch den gesamten Prozess begleiten.

- Interview-Flow : Feedback von Interviews schnell einsammeln, nachhalten und Stakeholder proaktiv erinnern.

- Active Sourcing : Kandidat:innen vor allem über LinkedIn finden, erste Profileinschätzungen machen und die Ansprache übernehmen - damit aus „spannend“ schnell ein Gespräch wird.

- Cross-functional Hiring supporten : Hiring über verschiedene Teams hinweg supporten (Product, Engineering, Operations, Commercial) und dabei unterschiedliche Anforderungen & Profile verstehen lernen.

- Team-Rituale & Ad-hoc : An Talent-Team-Routinen teilnehmen, Best Practices aufschnappen und spontan mit anpacken, wenn’s im Hiring gerade drauf ankommt

Wen wir suchen

- Eingeschriebenes Studium, Gap Year oder Phase zwischen zwei Studienabschnitten

- Lust darauf, Recruiting operativ stark aufzustellen und Hiring-Prozesse zu verbessern

- Hands-on-Mentalität sowie Freude daran, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und Themen verlässlich ins Ziel zu bringen

- Empathisches, souveränes und professionelles Auftreten gegenüber Kandidat:innen und Stakeholdern

- Strukturierte, detailgenaue Arbeitsweise mit gleichzeitigem Blick für das große Ganze

- Fähigkeit, Prioritäten zu setzen und Timings zu koordinieren

- Echtes Interesse an Menschen, Talent und Recruiting Operations

- Erste Berührungspunkte mit Tools wie Google Calendar oder hohe Lernbereitschaft im Umgang mit neuen Tools

- Affinität zu digitalen Tools und Automatisierung, um Recruiting smarter und effizienter zu gestalten

- Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und fließendes Englisch in Wort und Schrift

- Standort in Berlin und Lust auf Zusammenarbeit in einem schönen Office im Herzen der Stadt

Warum trawa?

Du hilfst dabei, die Zukunft der Energiebranche mitzugestalten – und übernimmst Verantwortung für Themen, die echten Impact haben: auf unsere Hiring-Qualität, unsere Kultur und unser Wachstum. Als Talent Acquisition Intern legst du mit uns die Grundlage für ein Team, das auf Top-Niveau liefert – und trägst damit direkt zu unserer Mission bei.

Was dich erwartet 

- Impact ab Tag 1 : Dein Beitrag beeinflusst Candidate Experience, unsere Talent Acquisition Prozesse und unsere Time-to-Hire spürbar

- Gestaltungsspielraum : Recruiting-Operations mit aufbauen, Ideen umsetzen – keine starren Prozesse, sondern Verbesserungskultur

- Onsite Zusammenarbeit: Unser Büro in Berlin-Mitte ist das Zentrum der Zusammenarbeit; Office-First-Kultur mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten

- Klarer Rahmen: Mindestens 3 Monate (idealerweise 6 Monate) mit Option auf Übernahme in eine Vollzeitrolle (FTE)

- Persönliche Entwicklung: End-to-end Recruiting lernen im Climate-Tech-Startup – Sourcing, Candidate Engagement, ATS-Hygiene, Prozess-Governance, Stakeholder Management

- Diversity & Inclusion : Alle sind willkommen – wir leben ein inklusives Arbeitsumfeld, das Vielfalt wertschätzt

Über uns

Willkommen im trawa-Universum! Unsere Mission ist es, den grünen Energieversorger der Zukunft von Grund auf zu bauen. Wie wir das schaffen? Wir ermöglichen B2B-Industrieunternehmen direkten Zugang zu erneuerbarer Energie, entwickeln Software und Technologie zur Steuerung der Volatilität an Energiemärkten und professionalisieren die Energiebeschaffung auf der Käuferseite.

description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

- ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

- High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're looking for a senior B2B Growth Marketer to build and scale demand generation for ElevenLabs in India. This is a hands-on, in-country role focused on generating enterprise pipeline, growing our brand with technical buyers, and creating programs that become benchmarks for B2B marketing in AI.

Your work will shape how Indian businesses discover, evaluate, and adopt ElevenLabs. The goal is to build repeatable marketing engines that make ElevenLabs the top choice for every enterprise.

What you'll do

- Build integrated B2B marketing campaigns end to end across India's priority industries from strategy and messaging through execution and measurement.

- Localize and execute programs across ABM, content, events, webinars, partner/customer marketing, executive branding, product launches, and outbound - choosing the right channel for the problem rather than owning a single function.

- Adapt global campaigns and messaging for the Indian market, and feed local insights (buyer behavior, competitive dynamics, regulatory context) back to the global team.

- Partner closely with local sales and the global product marketing, growth, and design teams to keep messaging consistent and execute high-impact campaigns.

- Own pipeline generation and campaign performance for the market, using data to measure results, run experiments, and continuously improve what works.

Requirements

- 5 to 7 years of experience at a high-growth technology company - you've built and scaled B2B demand generation programs that created measurable enterprise pipeline, and you know what moved the needle.

- Ownership Pedigree: You have implemented growth and marketing projects from start to finish and held yourself accountable for the ROI.

- Deep knowledge of the Indian market: its enterprise buyers, media landscape, and business culture, ideally with an existing network.

- Work well without much process. This role spans multiple marketing functions and needs someone who sets priorities, spots opportunities, and moves quickly as our first marketer in the market.

- Relentless commitment to excellence — a high bar for quality, clarity, and impact.

- Curious about AI, follows the technology ecosystem closely, and has exceptional judgment on what makes marketing stand out.

title: Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations [UK - Remote]
description:
Company Overview 

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm 

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.

The Role

As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

- Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

- Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

- Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

- Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives. 

- Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.

The Challenge

We are seeking researchers who:

- See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches

- Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months

- Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x

- Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact

If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.

It's Important to Us That You Have

- Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning

- Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities

- Proven ability to bridge theory and practice—someone who can both derive novel mathematical formulations and implement them efficiently

- Demonstrated ability to build data pipelines that can process and curate massive datasets while maintaining quality and diversity

- Track record of designing controlled experiments that isolate the impact of architectural innovations and validate theoretical insights

- Experience optimizing models for real-world deployment, including knowledge of hardware constraints and efficiency techniques

- History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI

Ideal Researcher Profile

An ideal researcher, as evidenced by the recurring themes across these foundational papers, excels in five key areas: (1) Statistical & Mathematical Foundations, (2) Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation, (3) Data-Driven & Scalable Systems, (4) Hardware & Systems Understanding, and (5) Rigorous Experimental Design. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models.

1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations 

Mastery of Core Concepts 

Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse.

Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways 

Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights.

Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing 

Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses.

2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation 

Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks 

Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts.

Turning Theory into Practice 

Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential.

Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source 

Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress.

3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems 

Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines 

Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models.

Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training 

A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance.

4. Hardware & Systems Understanding 

Efficient Implementations at Scale 

Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices.

Real-Time & On-Device Constraints 

SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness.

Architectural & Optimization Details 

Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency.

5. Rigorous Experimental Design 

Controlled Comparisons & Ablations 

Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter.

Multifold Evaluation Metrics 

From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics.

- Senior hiring : You have successfully recruited senior leaders and understand how sourcing, assessing and closing them differs from junior hiring.

- Judgment : You can distinguish exceptional people from candidates who simply have the right companies, titles or polish on their CV. You develop conviction quickly and can clearly articulate why someone does or does not meet the bar.

- Range : You can move between very different searches without losing depth. You learn unfamiliar markets quickly enough to recruit credibly within them.

- Only the paranoid survive : Bad sh*t is coming. By joining us, you're choosing to sail straight towards the storms with unhesitating conviction. However much we've already done, however far we've already come — it's still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist | Semiconductor Metrology 
Abingdon, UK

Reward and Benefits 

- £42,000 - £55,000 (depending on experience)

- Annual bonus, 3x salary death in service benefit and private health care BUPA, EMI Share scheme.

If you are a Data Scientist who enjoys turning instrument data into proof of what is possible, why not join us in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, and help prove the analysis methods behind advanced semiconductor metrology systems.

We are looking for an ambitious and adaptable Data Scientist to join our new Data Science team in the Technology department, reporting to the Data Science Lead and working closely with our Modelling Scientist. You will generate and curate data, develop and test new algorithms, and benchmark them against what the instrument can physically deliver. When a method proves itself, you will package it for the Data Analysis team in Engineering, who turn it into robust product software. You will work with real customer use cases and wafer data from Applications Development, and proof-of-concept data from R&D.

We are an AI-first team, so you will use AI tools every day, while checking carefully what they produce. If your passion is speed, evidence and finding out what the data can really tell you, we’d love to hear from you.

What you’ll be doing 

- Generate synthetic data, and build and maintain the demo and performance data libraries

- Analyse instrument data to quantify noise and limitations, and help establish the information limit, meaning what is physically extractable from the instrument

- Develop and test new algorithms and analysis methods (for example PCA, percentile methods and machine learning) on real and synthetic data

- Benchmark methods against the information limit: achievable performance, measurement uncertainty, gauge R&R and drift contributors

- Write clean, reproducible prototype code with test data and expected performance, ready to hand over to Data Analysis, and build analysis tools used across the Technology department

- Use AI tools every day to code, explore, analyse and report faster, verify what they produce, and present your results to the team

Education and experience 

- Degree or above in Physics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a similar subject, or [2] years’ relevant experience in data science or quantitative research

Skills and experience we’re looking for: 

- Data analysis in Python (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn or similar)

- Heavy, day-to-day use of AI tools in your technical work, such as coding assistants and LLMs, with the judgement to verify their outputs

- Image or signal processing, ideally on data from scientific instruments

- Statistics applied to measurement data: uncertainty, repeatability, noise and drift

- Machine learning methods, and how to validate them properly

- Clear, reproducible code and reports

- Explaining results to technical and non-technical colleagues

- Curious and adaptable, happy to work quickly and test ideas against the evidence

We’d love to see: 

- Atomic Force Microscopy or other nano-characterisation (SEM, FIB, profilometry), or semiconductor metrology

- Physics-based modelling or simulation

- Version control (Git) and C#, and experience building agentic or AI-assisted analysis workflows

A bit about us: 

Infinitesima is a privately owned company founded in 2001, as a spin-out of the University of Bristol, by CTO Professor Andrew Humphris. Our dynamic team of scientists and engineers is focussed on enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices through delivery of innovative products to customers around the world. 

Our strength lies in the varied perspectives that come from different cultures, experiences, and identities. We believe that true innovation is fuelled by collaboration, locally and globally. We strive to foster an environment where everyone can contribute meaningfully and thrive. If you require adjustments to take part in the recruitment process, please let us know, we’ll do our best to support you. 

Your recruitment journey: 

We will interview you: Monday to Friday UK Time 9am to 4.30pm and we'll be as flexible as we can with Global Scheduling 

1st stage: (45 minute) Remote meeting to evaluate your experience and technical ability 

2nd stage: (2.5 hours) Face to face onsite evaluating technical, presentation and communication skills along with your ways of working and your opportunity to to know more about us 

If you're not comfortable with eye contact, let us know at the start of your interview and if REMOTE, once we've said hello, feel free to turn your camera off until the end. 

We dress casually so informal attire is absolutely fine for onsite interviews. We want you to feel comfortable when you meet us and if there's anything else we can do to support your journey, just let us know. 

A note on how we use AI: 
We use AI only to transcribe our interviews so we can focus fully on you instead of scribbling notes. The AI does not take part in any decision making at any stage. All hiring decisions are made by real humans based on the conversation we have with you.

We recognise the value of flexibility and offer a hybrid working model wherever possible. Most employees work onsite three days per week, although some positions require a greater onsite presence due to the nature of the work and business need

We need engineers who can build the products, APIs and tools our customers use, and who understand the systems underneath well enough to make them work reliably in production.

This is a role for someone who takes a loosely defined problem, works out what the user actually needs, and owns the solution end to end. That means designing it, writing the code, shipping it, and debugging it when it breaks, without handing it off at the first layer boundary.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING 

Rather than a checklist, here’s what success in this role actually looks like:

- Own and drive user-facing products end to end, including web apps, APIs, backend services and CLI tools, mostly in Go. You’ll ship the simplest useful version first, then improve it based on how people actually use it.

- Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering & DevOps, Infrastructure & Data Centre Operations, Security and Customer Support. You’ll turn real customer problems into practical solutions.

- Build and maintain Kubernetes-based services, controllers and platform capabilities. This includes GPU scheduling and container runtimes.

- Identify repetitive operational work and replace it with automation, so software handles it instead of people.

- Investigate production issues across application code, Kubernetes, containers, Linux, networking, drivers and hardware. Each incident should end in a lasting fix, a guardrail or better tooling.

- Design services that behave well under load and during failure. You’ll instrument them so anyone can debug them, and give them secure defaults from day one.

- Contribute ideas and take ownership beyond your core remit. That includes product decisions on workflow and interface, such as whether a problem is best solved with a CLI, an API or a web experience.

ABOUT YOU 

We care more about how you think and work than a perfect CV. You’ll likely bring a combination of the following:

Essential: 

- Strong professional experience building, debugging and operating production software in Go. Deep experience in another systems language also works, if you can show you’d become productive in Go quickly.

- Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and containers, including how workloads are scheduled, how services communicate, and how to investigate when things misbehave.

- Confidence in Linux environments: systemd, processes, signals, filesystems, permissions, networking, and CPU and memory diagnostics.

- A track record of systems, products or tools you personally designed and built.

- Solid engineering fundamentals: concurrency, API and interface design, and failure modes. You’ll also have practical experience troubleshooting production systems with logs, metrics and system-level tooling.

Nice to Have: 

- Familiarity with the NVIDIA GPU ecosystem, such as drivers, CUDA, nvidia-smi, GPU-enabled container runtimes or Kubernetes GPU scheduling. This isn’t essential: strong systems debugging and a genuine interest in learning this area count just as much.

- Experience with distributed and event-driven systems, such as queues, retries, idempotency and backpressure. Practical networking knowledge (DNS, TCP/IP, HTTP, load balancing) also helps.

- Experience building Kubernetes controllers or operators, or developer tooling used by other engineers. A security-minded approach to auth, secrets and attack surfaces is a plus.

WHAT WE OFFER 

- Competitive salary and annual discretionary bonus scheme

- Employee wellbeing benefits

- 25 days holiday, plus public holidays

- Private Medical Insurance

- Enhanced Pension Scheme

- Flexible working arrangements (remote or hybrid, depending on role and location)

- Real ownership and autonomy — the trust to take initiative and experiment

- Visible, meaningful impact as we scale

- Clear career progression in a high-growth company

- A collaborative, international culture built on trust, transparency, and ownership

- The chance to help shape NexGen Cloud’s team, culture, and future

WHY APPLY 

We welcome applications from all backgrounds. If you enjoy solving complex infrastructure problems and want to build something meaningful at scale, we’d like to hear from you.

MORE INFORMATION 

Visit our careers page to learn more about us or follow us on LinkedIn and X to learn more about our journey and keep up with our latest news and releases.

Your market is two-sided. You open net-new accounts that fit our ideal customer profile and have never spoken to us, and you turn low-adoption customers who use a single Lighthouse product into full-platform customers. In both cases the goal is the same: the whole commercial platform, not one module. Small, one-off transactions are not what this role is for. You think in terms of the full deal from the first conversation, and you have the patience and the process to run a complex, multi-stakeholder cycle to get there. 

What makes this different: you won’t do it alone. Lighthouse is deploying an agent AI infrastructure — Enablement, Pre-Sales, and Coaching agents — alongside a modern revenue stack. AI handles the prep, the sequencing, and the pattern recognition so you can focus on what matters — building relationships, running sharp discovery, and closing deals. 

Where you will have impact 

Own your territory and your number. Build and execute a strategic territory plan to generate a net-new pipeline. Maintain 3x pipeline coverage, forecast honestly, and take full accountability for your results. Your quota is your commitment. 

Hunt into net-new accounts. Cold, outbound prospecting into ideal customer profile accounts is the core of this role, not a supplement to inbound. Run an AI-first workflow: use our agents for account research, buying signals, sequencing and first-touch personalization, so your time goes into conversations rather than admin. Expand low-adoption customers. Identify customers who use a single Lighthouse product, or a fraction of what they bought, and turn them into full-platform accounts. Run this as a sales cycle, with discovery, a business case and a close, not as an adoption program. Work with Customer Success on the handover so the account is set up to keep growing. 

Turn small deals into big deals. Treat every opportunity as a platform deal. Qualify for the full scope early, bring in every stakeholder who has a say, and build the business case for the whole solution rather than settling for a trial or a single module. Protect pricing on value. 

Run a disciplined sales process. Using MEDDPICC to qualify and advance opportunities. Use the AI Pre-Sales Agent to identify gaps before every major call. Advance deals through stage gates with evidence, not optimism. Leverage AI to make your days easier and focus on more selling time. 

Use AI as a force multiplier. Leverage the Enablement Agent for call prep, discovery frameworks, and positioning. Use the Coaching Agent to surface patterns in your pipeline and win rate. Push back on the tools when they’re wrong — help make the system smarter. 

Become a hospitality expert. Understand the commercial challenges hotels face across pricing, distribution, and business intelligence. Position Lighthouse’s full platform as the integrated solution that replaces fragmented point tools. Know the competitive landscape inside out and run value based ROI conversations confidently. 

Build relationships at a distance. Most of your buyers will never meet you in person. Earn trust over video, phone and email through sharp preparation, clear follow-through and a point of view on their business. Partner with Product to share market feedback and influence the roadmap, and represent Lighthouse at industry events to build the brand and your network.

You’ll join a global Revenue team of 150+ sales professionals across 24 countries. The Acquisition team is where new revenue starts: we open the accounts the rest of the company grows. We work across the full Lighthouse product suite, helping hotels, chains, and hospitality groups achieve their commercial goals. - Impactful work: Shape products relied on by 85,000+ users worldwide. 

- Wellbeing support: Subsidized up to 80% ClassPass subscription. 

- Referral bonuses: Earn rewards for bringing in new talent. 

- Additional maternity leave compensation: For the first 12 weeks of Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), we top-up your SMP so that your salary reaches 100% 

Who you are 

- 2–5 years in a closing sales role, SaaS experience is a must but hunger and skill matters more than industry tenure. 

- A hunter by instinct. You prospect cold, you get past no, and you would rather build your own pipeline than wait for it.

- E xceptional command of the English language. 

- Strong business acumen with the ability to sell on value, not price. Confident engaging stakeholders from GMs to C-suite. 

- You want to win, and you like it when people notice. You celebrate your wins and your team’s, you prospect when it would be easier not to, you follow up one more time, and you’re not okay with a bad quarter. 

Diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging 

Thank you for considering a career with Lighthouse. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace that values equal opportunity for all. title: Head of India
description:
The Role 

India is the biggest remittance market with over $130 billion a year flowing home to it, from everywhere: engineers in the Bay Area and Sydney, cabbies in Toronto, construction crews in Dubai, shopkeepers in Leicester, students in Berlin. From Punjabis, Gujaratis, Tamils, Malayalis and Telugus. From people wiring $3,000 a month to a Mumbai mortgage and people sending $80 to a village in Bihar. Your job is to win this market.

You are someone who gets excited by the nuances of the Indian diaspora and how to reach each group, and who wants to own the P&L, the regulatory landscape and pricing at the same time. If you find the price sensitivity of each cohort exciting, and "why do Malayali nurses cluster in specific hospital systems, and what does that mean for acquisition?" as interesting as "what's RBI's latest remittance policy and which banks make the best partners," this is it.

As the GM, you own the P&L, and set pricing. For customer growth, you decide which communities to acquire and in what order. Know the RBI's rules well enough to see the openings inside them, not just the limits. A Gujarati family in New Jersey and a Punjabi trucker in Brampton got abroad through completely different networks, and reaching them takes completely different channels.

Reports to the Head of South Asia. Builds a team of FX Advisors in India and growth managers in sending markets. The face of India inside and outside the company. Total ownership. Be your own CEO

What You'll Own 

- The P&L. Volume, gross profit and CAC across every India corridor. Not influence, own. A miss is your miss. A beat is your win.

- Strategy and sequencing. Which sender markets, which communities, which channels, in what order. US, Canada, UK, Europe, Australia and UAE to start. Build the plan, defend it to leadership, execute it.

- Pricing. India is the most rate-sensitive, most competitive remittance market in the world, up against competitors who reprice daily. Set FX and fee strategy corridor by corridor.

- The regulatory and partner landscape. RBI rules, bank partnerships, payout rails. Know the terrain cold and own the local relationships.

- Product. Obsess over UX and the services NRIs actually need. Closer to the customer than anyone in the company, and what you hear feeds straight into product, pricing and customer support.

- The diaspora puzzle. Community partnerships, temples and gurdwaras and churches, cricket leagues, student associations, remittance-heavy employers, influencers, festivals (Diwali is a season, not a day). Get in front of each community authentically, and cheaply.

- The team. Hire, coach and retain people in India and in sending markets. Small, dense, fast.

Who You Are 

- 10 to 15 years in high-growth environments: startups, operations, consulting, finance, fintech. Has owned a number and talks about it the way owners do.

- Diaspora-fluent. Real knowledge of and networks in the Indian diaspora, and real curiosity about it. Migration patterns, community structures, who sends money to whom and why.

- Commercially sharp. Holds pricing, unit economics and CAC math in their head, and works the data directly. Excel or Sheets required, SQL a real plus.

- A hustler with judgment. Closes a bank partnership Monday, reviews corridor margins Tuesday, shows up at a community event in Jackson Heights on Saturday. Likes all three.

- A regulatory realist. Understands (or can quickly master) RBI rules and the compliance realities of moving money into India. Treats compliance as a partner, not an obstacle.

- Multilingual, ideally. Fluent in English. Hindi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu or Malayalam are genuine assets.

Location: London or Dubai. Regular travel to India and sending markets is part of the job.

Why This Role 

India is the largest remittance market in the world, and winning it moves the whole company forward. This role owns that outcome, with the authority and the accountability that come with it. It also drives real value for the customers: Immigrants work hard for this money, and every basis point saved goes home.

The role 

We are formalising our security assurance function. We have technical controls and the engineering culture; what we need now is the governance layer that proves it - to our auditors, to our funders, and to our regulator.

You will be the delivery engine behind that. You will own the recurring assurance cycle end to end, run our third-party security programme, and be the person who turns evidence into something a due diligence team or a certification auditor can be satisfied by.

You will be responsible for building controls, gathering evidence, and challenging suppliers.

What you will own: 

1. Third-party security assurance 

- Run security due diligence on new suppliers, maintain initial questionnaire to risk sign-off, working with Procurement and Legal on security and data protection schedules.

- Maintain a supplier tiering model based on criticality and run the periodic re-assessment cycle for tiered suppliers: certification expiry, subprocessor changes, breach notifications, SLA performance.

- Maintain the supplier and outsourcing registers, including preparation for the FCA's material third party register under PS26/2 (rules in force 18 March 2027).

- Track concentration risk and exit plans for critical suppliers.

2. Inbound due diligence and customer assurance 

- Own our response to security due diligence from funders, banking partners, institutional investors, commercial partners and prospects.

- Build and maintain a reusable trust pack: answer library, security whitepaper, current certifications, pen test attestations, standard questionnaire pre-fills (SIG, CAIQ).

- Turn a 40-hour bespoke questionnaire response into a 4-hour one.

3. The assurance calendar 

- Maintain the annual calendar of security activities and make sure each one happens, produces evidence, and closes its actions: penetration tests, access reviews, disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, policy reviews, supplier re-assessments, awareness training.

- Coordinate external penetration tests: scoping, vendor selection, scheduling, findings triage, remediation tracking, retest.

- Facilitate tabletop exercises, including scenario design and post-exercise action tracking.

4. Risk and control administration 

- Maintain the information security risk register: run the assessment cycle, record treatment plans with named owners and dates, chase closure.

- Administer the policy exception and risk acceptance process, ensuring every exception is owned, time-bound and reviewed on expiry.

- Perform first-line control testing: sample-test where key controls operate as designed and retain the evidence.

- Produce security MI for the Head of Security to take to ExCo and the Risk Committee.

5. Vulnerability and findings management 

- Consolidate findings across sources — EDR, cloud security posture, SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets scanning, penetration tests — into a single view with agreed severity definitions and remediation SLAs.

- Triage, route and chase remediation with engineering teams; escalate ageing findings.

- Own the reporting on remediation performance.

6. Security awareness 

- Run the awareness programme: induction, annual refresher, phishing simulation, role-based training for engineers, completion tracking.

- Coordinate pre-employment screening with People.

What you will contribute to: 

- The ISO 27001 ISMS , which we are building towards certification. You will draft and maintain control documentation, populate the Statement of Applicability, gather evidence, coordinate the internal audit programme and be a primary point of contact for our external auditor. The Head of Security owns the framework, scope, and risk appetite.

- Policies and standards: you will draft, review and shepherd policies through approval, and track the review cycle.

- Incident response: you will maintain the IR plan and playbooks, facilitate post-incident reviews, track remediation actions, and support regulatory notification (ICO personal data breach reporting within 72 hours; FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15.3).

- Business continuity and DR: you will maintain the documentation and the testing evidence.

- Secure development: you will help embed security requirements into the SDLC and support threat modelling sessions.

- Data protection: you will support RoPA maintenance, DPIA completion and DSAR handling alongside Legal.

What success looks like: 

First 90 days: you know our supplier estate and have tiered it; the assurance calendar for the next 12 months is published and owned; inbound due diligence requests come to you and go out without the Head of Security rewriting them.

Six months: the trust pack exists and is being used; the risk register is live with owned treatment plans; ISO 27001 evidence collection is systematic rather than a scramble; the exception register exists.

Twelve months: supplier re-assessment runs on a cadence without prompting; the material third party register is ready ahead of the March 2027 deadline; MI to the Risk Committee is trusted.

Essential experience: 

- Three or more years in an information security assurance, GRC or security compliance role, at least some of it in a regulated financial services environment or another environment with real external audit pressure.

- Hands-on experience of ISO 27001, whether operating an ISMS or taking one through certification.

- Demonstrable experience running third-party or vendor security assessments, and of responding to inbound security due diligence.

- Comfortable reading technical findings — an EDR vulnerability report, a penetration test finding, a cloud misconfiguration — and forming your own view on severity and real-world exploitability rather than passing the vendor's rating through unchanged.

- Clear, concise written English. Much of this role is writing things that external parties will judge us on.

- The confidence to chase a busy engineer, challenge a supplier's assertion, and tell us when an answer is not good enough.

Desirable: 

- Experience of a cloud-native environment, ideally AWS.

- Experience of scaling a control framework as an organisation grows.

- Familiarity with UK operational resilience expectations (SYSC 15A) and outsourcing requirements (SYSC 8).

description:
About Abound 

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.

Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

The Role 

We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen.

This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off.

We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you.

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

What you'll be doing 

- Own the Express / Mid-prime product: proposition, roadmap, performance and economics, with direct accountability for the balance between growth and credit quality.

- Lead how we quote and present offers across aggregator and price-comparison marketplaces, optimising eligibility, risk-based pricing and offer presentation to win the right customers at the point of acquisition.

- Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book.

- Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

- Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

- Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

- Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

- Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science.

- Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

- Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

- Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

- Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

Who you are 

- A product person at heart: you care about the customer, the journey and the commercial outcome, and you want to own something end to end.

- Quantitative and hands-on. You are comfortable in SQL and Python (or similar), you can interrogate a dataset yourself, and you can hold your own in a conversation with data scientists about model performance and calibration.

- Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending.

- Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance.

- Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth.

- Able to move between detail and direction: happy getting into the data on a Tuesday and shaping the roadmap on a Wednesday.

- Confident challenging assumptions and turning analysis into practical action, and able to explain your reasoning clearly to people who are not analysts.

- Collaborative and credible with risk, commercial, engineering and data science teams.

- Structured, proactive and comfortable in a scaling environment where priorities evolve quickly and ownership is expected.

Experience and background 

- Around four to five years of experience in product, credit strategy, analytics or a closely related role within consumer lending or fintech. We are deliberately targeting this level: this is a step-up role for someone ready to own a product, not a lateral move for someone who has run several.

- Experience in unsecured consumer lending, ideally Unsecured Personal Loans (UPL), with exposure to the mechanics of acquiring customers through price-comparison or aggregator marketplaces. Direct experience in higher-APR or near-prime lending is a strong plus but not a prerequisite.

- Hands-on data skills: SQL as a minimum, and ideally Python or R for analysis. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be able to work alongside them as a peer and do your own analysis.

- Experience working with or alongside credit decisioning, scorecards or risk models, and an understanding of how they are built, monitored and adjusted for a specific population.

- Some experience of pricing, eligibility or offer design, and of using experiments or A/B tests to evaluate changes.

- A track record of using analysis to influence decisions, not just to report on outcomes, in a role where you had some accountability for commercial results.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to senior stakeholders.

- Experience with Open Banking data or cashflow underwriting is a plus, as is experience in a fast-growing fintech.

Salary up to £85,000 DOE, plus a Welcome Bonus of up to £3,000 and a Relocation Allowance of up to £5,000

This is a rare opportunity to step into a true leadership role while staying close to what you love most, delivering excellent clinical care.

This role offers the best of both worlds. Around 80% of your time will be spent in practice, working across a varied and rewarding caseload, from consults to surgery. Alongside this, you will play a key leadership role, supporting and developing your colleagues, guiding clinical discussions and helping to build confidence in less experienced vets and new graduates.

You’ll also have the opportunity to influence how the practice grows and evolves, contributing to clinical standards, continuous improvement and a strong, collaborative culture across two busy sites.

You’ll be joining a genuinely friendly, experienced and supportive team of vets, RVNs and client care colleagues who enjoy working together and supporting one another. The practice is well equipped, with digital and dental X-ray, ultrasound and multiparameter monitoring, giving you everything you need to deliver high-quality care.

All of this is set in the beautiful Yorkshire countryside, within easy reach of bustling cities such as York, Harrogate and Selby. The outdoors is your thing? No problem – the North York Moors, Howardian Hills, Yorkshire Wolds and the East Coast are on your doorstep. Public transport links and motorway connections are in easy reach. Overall, an exceptional place to live and work.

How You’ll Make a Difference 

This role offers the best of both worlds. Around 80% of your time will be spent in practice, working across a varied and rewarding caseload, from consults to surgery. Alongside this, you will play a key leadership role, supporting and developing your colleagues, guiding clinical discussions and helping to build confidence in less experienced vets and new graduates.

You’ll also have the opportunity to influence how the practice grows and evolves, contributing to clinical standards, continuous improvement and a strong, collaborative culture across two busy sites.

You’ll set and execute the strategic direction of the practices, lead multidisciplinary teams, and ensure the delivery of high standards across operations, client experience and business performance. This role plays a critical part in shaping culture, driving results and supporting sustainable growth.

Working Pattern 

* Working 40 hours per week across either 4 or 5 days

* Working a share of one in four Saturday mornings

* No out-of-hours or on-call commitments.

You Might Be a Great Fit If...

You are a senior operational leader with strong commercial acumen and a people-centred leadership approach. You’ll bring:

* Proven experience in a senior or leadership role within veterinary practice

* Strong clinical expertise with the confidence to support complex case discussions and decision-making

* A collaborative and people-focused leadership style, with experience mentoring and developing others

* The ability to drive clinical standards, governance, and continuous improvement

* Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills

How We’ll Support You

At inspiring vet care, we’re committed to supporting you in a senior executive leadership role. When you join us, you’ll benefit from:

* Overall leadership of a practice or hospital with the autonomy to shape strategy, culture and performance

* Senior-level influence across operations, client experience and business outcomes

* Opportunities to lead large-scale change and drive long-term organisational impact

* Ongoing learning and development to support executive and leadership growth

* A collaborative, values-led culture focused on care, community and continuous improvement

* 6.6 weeks’ holiday including bank holidays

* Private medical insurance

* Enhanced family leave and pay across maternity, paternity, adoption and surrogacy

* Pension scheme

* Retail discounts and cashback offers

* Reduced-cost veterinary care for your own pets

We’re committed to supporting our people through career development opportunities, wellbeing initiatives and access to world-class learning resources.

Whether you’re just starting out or looking to take the next step in your career, inspiring vet care offers the support, opportunity and community to help you grow.

title: Clinical Director - Equine

With strong foundations, an excellent reputation and a committed clinical team, the practice is well positioned for its next chapter. * A genuinely hands-on leadership role within a close-knit, experienced team

* Maintain an active clinical caseload aligned with your interests and strengths

If you value space, spectacular landscapes and outdoor living alongside a rewarding veterinary career, this is a unique opportunity to enjoy both.

You Might Be a Great Fit If...

You are a senior clinical leader with strong equine expertise, commercial awareness and a passion for developing people and services. You'll bring:

* Significant experience as an Equine Veterinary Surgeon, ideally with advanced qualifications such as CertAVP or equivalent

* Proven leadership experience with responsibility for supporting and developing veterinary teams

* Strong commercial and financial awareness with an interest in practice performance and sustainability

* Experience contributing to clinical governance, audit and continuous improvement initiatives

* Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder management skills

* A collaborative, values-led leadership style with a commitment to exceptional patient and client care

How We'll Support You

At inspiring vet care, we're committed to supporting you in a senior clinical leadership role. When you join us, you'll benefit from:

* A senior leadership position with genuine autonomy and influence over the future direction of the practice

* Clear career pathways into wider clinical and operational leadership opportunities

* Ongoing leadership development and access to the inspiring vet care Academy

title: Senior Sales Development Representative  - (Remote)
description:

- Pipeline review with weekly team meeting 

- Other duties as assigned.

- Minimum of 5 years related work experience; bachelor's degree preferred.

- Consistent track record of meeting and exceeding lead generation and new account development objectives.

- Fluent English and G erman or French preferred but not essential 

- Excellent communication skills in writing, speaking, listening, and outbound calling - able to communicate clearly, concisely, and with precision.

- Ability to understand and successfully promote technical offerings and solution sets, supported by strong curiosity about business problems and product value.

- Ability to prioritize work assignments and shift efforts based on business goals and team needs.

- 4 recharge days, where the entire company goes on a brief pause in all geographies for 1 day each quarter. This day can be spent in whatever way helps you recharge, to regain energy, and dive back into the next workday

- Accident Insurance

Vendavo partners with the world’s leading companies to accelerate growth and profitability, advance innovation, and build more prosperous communities. title: Regional Operations Manager - Data Centre / Hyper-scale / Co-location expertise
description:
As our Regional Operations Manager, you’ll be responsible for leading, coordinating, and delivering commissioning and technical operations across multiple projects within their assigned regions in mainland Europe. 

You will ensure that all technical, operational, and delivery activities are executed safely, efficiently, consistently, and in line with company standards, contractual requirements, and client expectations. 

You will provide technical authority, operational leadership, and oversight of site-based teams, acting as the primary link between regional project delivery and senior management. 

It is essential that you have the flexibility to travel into Europe every week or ideally you will be already based in Europe with the flexibility to travel around EU without restrictions. 

Key Areas of Responsibility 

Technical Leadership 

- Provide technical leadership, direction, and oversight to all site-based commissioning and operations teams within the region. 

- Act as the senior technical authority for commissioning activities on assigned projects. 

- Set and enforce technical standards, methodologies, and best practices across all sites. 

- Lead by example through active participation in technical discussions, troubleshooting, and decision-making. 

- Support site teams in resolving complex commissioning, integration, and performance issues. 

Project and Operational Management 

- Work closely with Project Managers and key stakeholders to define project scope, milestones, and deliverables. 

- Develop, monitor, and maintain regional delivery plans, schedules, and resource forecasts. 

- Ensure projects are delivered in line with contractual, technical, and commercial requirements. 

- Oversee progress, risks, and constraints, implementing corrective actions where required. 

- Ensure consistency of execution and reporting across all projects in the region. 

Technical Governance and Quality 

- Ensure that all commissioning activities comply with company procedures, industry standards, and client requirements. 

- Review, approve, and contribute to technical documentation, including test procedures, commissioning plans, reports, and handover documentation. 

- Ensure technical risks are identified, managed, and mitigated. 

- Support audits, quality reviews, and lessons-learned activities across the region. 

Client and Stakeholder Engagement 

- Act as a senior technical and operational point of contact for clients within the region. 

- Understand client technical requirements and ensure they are incorporated into project delivery. 

- Provide clear, accurate, and timely communication on progress, risks, and technical matters. 

- Manage client expectations and contribute to maintaining high levels of client satisfaction. 

- Support the resolution of client issues and escalation of major concerns. 

Continuous Improvement and Industry Awareness 

- Stay informed of industry trends, emerging technologies, and commissioning best practices. 

- Drive improvements in tools, processes, and methodologies across the region. 

- Support the development and refinement of company technical and operational standards 

Health, Safety and Compliance 

- Ensure that all operations are carried out in compliance with health, safety, environmental, and company policies. 

- Promote a strong safety culture across all sites. 

- Ensure that risks are assessed and controlled before and during all site activities. 

This outlines the principal responsibilities and accountabilities of the role. It is not intended to be exhaustive, and the post holder may be required to undertake other duties commensurate with the level of responsibility and within their competence to support the wider organisation. 

Education 

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Electrical, Mechanical, Building Services, or related engineering discipline. 

- Postgraduate qualification in Engineering or Project / Operations Management is desirable. 

- Formal training or certification in data centre or mission-critical commissioning, project management, and health & safety is desirable. 

Skills and Experience (Data Centre Commissioning) 

- Strong technical knowledge of mission-critical data centre systems, including electrical power, mechanical cooling, controls, and integrated systems. 

- Proven experience leading data centre commissioning activities, including Level 1–5 commissioning and Integrated Systems Testing (IST). 

- Sound understanding of redundancy, resilience, and maintainability concepts (N, N+1, 2N). 

- Ability to review, approve, and author commissioning plans, test procedures, and handover documentation. 

- Experience managing commissioning activities in live or operational data centre environments. 

- Knowledge of relevant data centre standards and frameworks (e.g. Tier concepts, EN 50600, TIA-942). 

- Strong leadership and coordination skills across multi-disciplinary teams and multiple sites. 

- Effective communication skills with clients, contractors, and internal stakeholders. 

- Structured approach to risk management, technical problem-solving, and decision making. 

Why Join Global Commissioning? 

- Work on large-scale, high-profile data centre projects across Europe 

- Take a senior leadership role in a growing specialist organisation 

- Contribute to the development of commissioning standards and best practice 

- Join a collaborative and technically driven team environment 

- Due to frequent travel across Europe, the role is open to candidates based anywhere in the UK, preferably near a major UK international airport.
