title: Senior Fleet Manager
Go-To-Market Associate
description:
About us 

Hey there! We're Lleverage, and we're making the Autonomous Back Office actually achievable for businesses. We enable teams to capture, automate, and integrate AI agents into their business, because AI is only useful when it actually fits into daily operations. 

We help the most strategic European industries – manufacturing, logistics, and wholesale – automate the messy, manual processes that most tools can’t handle. 

We’re a fast-growing, VC-backed scale-up based in Amsterdam, with big ambitions for 2026 and beyond. This is your chance to join early, have real impact, and grow alongside the company. If that sounds something you want to help build, we'd love to have you on board! 

About the role 

We're looking for an exceptional Go-To-Market Associate who will be the engine of our commercial team. As part of the top 1% of Commercial talents globally, you'll combine systematic prospecting with creative outreach to build relationships with decision-makers who need AI solutions. 

This is not a classic sales role. We're looking for a builder with a commercial brain and an enormous drive, someone who combines hustle, strategic creativity, and genuine curiosity about what makes businesses tick. 

You might come from a classic sales background, or you might have built your commercial instincts in a completely different arena. What matters far more than your CV is your drive, your entrepreneurial instinct, and the kind of work ethic that makes people wonder how you get so much done. 

In a single day you might: map a new industry vertical for outreach opportunities, run a consultative discovery call with a Head of Operations at a manufacturing company, develop a proposal for a new channel, follow up on an active deal in scoping, and draft a business case for entering a completely new market. 

You won't have a large team behind you. You will have full autonomy, meaningful equity, direct access to the founding team, and the freedom to experiment with what works. 

Why Lleverage? 

- Change the world, literally : 2026 is the year AI works, and Lleverage.ai has the best AI platform (according to industry veterans) 

- Work, learn, have fun : You'll be part of a top-notch commercial team that operates at the highest level of performance 

- Build a unique network : Connect with decision-makers and operational leaders across traditional industries who are eager to implement AI solutions 

- Get autonomy & ownership : Design your own strategies and own your pipeline development 

- Compensation : We pay top of market cash and equity, with compensation tied to the pipeline value you create 

Responsibilities 

- Own our top of funnel: which segments we go after, how we reach the COOs and CFOs of manufacturers and distributors, and how many qualified opportunities land in the pipeline every week. That's your number. 

- Sit in on live deals from day one : discovery calls, account plans, proposals and PoC scoping with our delivery team. Within 6 to 12 months you run your first deals yourself. 

- Build the playbook with the GTM lead and CCO: positioning per sector, messaging per persona, pricing experiments, the business cases we win with. 

- Run experiments across the whole funnel: outbound campaigns, events, partnerships with ERP partners and PE firms, LinkedIn content. Measure everything, scale what works. 

- Use AI-native tooling (Clay, lemlist, our own agents) to research, personalise and scale what a team of five used to do by hand, and help us figure out what GTM looks like when AI does the grunt work. 

- Bring what you see in the market to the founding team and product: which use cases, sectors, competitors and prices we should bet on next. 

Job specific requirements 

- 1 to 3 years in consulting, investment banking, PE or a fast-growing B2B startup, or you built something yourself. 

- You make things happen without a brief, and can show it with an example and a number. 

- You win trust fast, with a CFO in a boardroom and with an operations manager on a factory floor. 

- You think in funnels and business cases and turn data into a clear recommendation. 

- New sectors, no playbook, channels nobody has tried: that energises you rather than stops you. A no on Monday doesn't define your Tuesday. 

- Genuinely curious about how businesses make money and where they lose it. 

- You want to own revenue within a year and know why. 

- Fluent Dutch and English, German is a big plus 

Nice to haves 

- Worked with or for manufacturing, wholesale, logistics or food companies. 

- Hands-on with HubSpot, Clay or lemlist. 

- Understanding of ERP-driven processes (SAP, Business Central, Exact). 

- Sold something before: side business, campus sales, fundraising. 

Our Tech Stack 

You'll be working with best-in-class tools: 

- CRM : HubSpot for pipeline management 

- Prospecting : AI-powered research and outreach tools like Clay and Lemlist 

- Communication : Multi-channel outreach across email, LinkedIn, and phone 

- Analytics : Data-driven insights to optimize your approach 

- And always exploring what's next 

We offer 

You are ready for the ride of a lifetime with experienced entrepreneurs and innovators who aim for hyper growth on a global scale. We look for an enormous drive and hands-on mentality. Somebody who can work with us in creating the best AI platform out there! 

We offer a good salary, a highly experienced (and very entertaining...) team and considerable share and bonus packages. And last but not least, this is the start of your career to grow to into a commercial lead and to lay the foundation for years to come.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
In a world where geopolitical tensions and security threats are accelerating, the way nations protect people and preserve peace is being redefined. For a long time, innovating in defense was about making tougher hardware. But with the evolution of software and the recent AI disruption, the future of defense is shifting to software-powered unmanned systems that save lives by removing humans from the front line. This is our mission.

At Intelic, we're building the intelligence layer for unmanned systems in defense. As a software-first company, we enable autonomous platforms to operate together - faster, smarter, and more reliably - across complex, mission-critical environments. Our technology turns disconnected assets into coordinated forces, helping operators make accurate decisions when it matters most.

Based in Amsterdam and growing fast, Intelic offers a rare opportunity to work on products that don't just move metrics - they meaningfully impact safety, resilience, and the future of Europe's security.

Why This Role Exists

Nexus has to run in places most software never goes: offline, in the field, installed and operated by people who are not developers. Getting it there in one piece, and keeping it running, is a job on its own.

Right now that job sits mostly with three backend engineers who cover this alongside their own work. As Nexus grows, so does the team, and we're adding someone to take real ownership of the pipelines, installers, and infrastructure that turn Nexus into something operators can trust, and who treats security as part of how the work gets done, not a separate project bolted on afterwards.

What You Will Do

You will join Product Adoption, the team that owns the last stretch between working software and a field-ready product: deployment, installers, monitoring, and everything that keeps Nexus running once it leaves the building. We are hiring at medior to senior level, roughly a 2 to 3, with room to flex higher for the right person.

- Build and maintain the CI/CD pipelines that turn Nexus into an installable, field-ready product across Linux and Windows

- Maintain and harden our software supply chain, including dependency scanning and package security

- Own the Windows installer and service orchestration, and help developers debug the platform-specific issues that come with it: permissions, firewalls, services, "works on my machine"

- Secure the software update server, the one online touchpoint in an otherwise offline system, and keep telemetry from the field reliable without leaking sensitive data

- Harden APIs and authentication on the surfaces that face the outside world

- Maintain and gradually take over our on-prem infrastructure: physical servers, backups, and disaster recovery, as we move away from renting machines in the cloud

- Build small internal tools, mostly in Python, Rust and shell or PowerShell scripts: installers, updaters, and the occasional internal or customer-facing web app

- Support incident response when things break in production, and help build the monitoring that catches problems before customers do

- Write down what you learn, so the next person, including future you, doesn't have to debug the same thing twice

You'll Thrive Here If

- You bring solid experience with CI/CD pipelines and build automation

- Comfort working across both Linux and Windows, with the ability to actually debug problems on either, not just deploy to them

- Experience with infrastructure as code (Ansible, OpenTofu, or similar)

- A security mindset: hardening, secure defaults, and attack surface are just part of how you build things, not an afterthought

- Enough scripting or programming ability to read and contribute to Python, Rust, or shell scripts. There is there is plenty of custom tooling to build.

- A level head under pressure. You can prioritise and stay steady when a few things break at once

Nice to have: 

- Experience with on-prem, bare-metal or virtulized infrastructure, not just cloud consoles

- Familiarity with Docker

- Exposure to dependency and package scanning tools such as Sonatype

- An interest in platform or infrastructure engineering as its own discipline. We expect this to split into a dedicated function over time

- Ability to build in-house tooling where needed and integrate vendor solutions where they fit

What Your First Year Will Look Like

- You've taken over meaningful parts of the CI/CD pipeline and installer work independently, without needing step-by-step instructions

- You've hardened at least one exposed surface end to end, the update server, an API, or similar

- You've helped move part of our infrastructure off rented machines and onto hardware we run ourselves

- Developers come to you when something breaks on Windows or Linux, because you've built a track record of finding the actual root cause

- You've documented enough of what you know that the team is less dependent on any one person, including you

Why Intelic

- We are setting up an environment, largely from the ground up that has to approved by MoDs

- You won't be bored. New projects, new problems, and a steady stream of things nobody has solved here before

- Real ownership from day one, not ticket-taking. If you see a better tool or approach, you're free to try it

- You'll work with hardware that matters: servers you can walk up to, deployments running in places with no internet, problems that cloud-only engineers rarely see

- A small team that leans on each other. When someone's on leave, the rest pick up the slack, and vice versa

- The mission is real. Nexus supports operators in the field, and how well you build and secure it has a direct effect on whether it works when it counts

What We Offer

- Stock Appreciation Rights programme (equity)

- A vibrant office at NDSM Plein, Amsterdam Noord — where we come together in person every day, because we believe it matters for the kind of work we do

- Flexible pension plan

- 25 vacation days

- Travel allowance

- Urban Sports corporate membership

- Lease a Bike option

Please note that, as part of our recruitment process, we may request a Certificate of Conduct (VOG) and conduct a background screening in accordance with our screening policy. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this process.

title: Senior Backend Engineer (Rust)
description:
About Intelic 

In a world where geopolitical tensions and security threats are accelerating, the way nations protect people and preserve peace is being redefined. At Intelic, we're building the intelligence layer for unmanned systems in defense: software that enables autonomous platforms to operate together, faster, smarter, and more reliably, across complex, mission-critical environments.

Based in Amsterdam and growing fast, we offer a rare opportunity to work on products that don't just move metrics. They directly affect safety, resilience, and Europe's security.

Why the role exists 

Our drones carry more and more hardware: cameras, gimbals, servos and more. The European market is fragmented, so we need to support many different types of hardware. Right now, adding a new piece of hardware usually means our own engineers have to integrate it. We want to change that. We're building a platform that lets partners and other teams connect their own hardware and write their own driver.

You'll work alongside robotics engineers and help set the team up from the start. The APIs and system design you create will be what everyone else builds on.

If you like hard backend problems where good design directly affects how fast other people can move, this role is worth a look.

What you will do 

You'll spend most of your time in Rust, working out how to abstract the communication with the hardware from the rest of the system. That could mean designing how a new camera gets configured through the API, or writing a simulated camera so you can test an integration before the hardware is on your desk.

- Design and build the platform in Rust

- Define the APIs that other teams and partners use to integrate cameras, gimbals, servos and other hardware

- Make it possible for others to write their own drivers and add hardware without needing support from your team

- Think through how each new module fits into the wider system, and plan for the cases others will run into later

- Write strong unit tests and add integration tests, including tests against simulated hardware

- Work directly with other teams to understand what they need from the platform and agree on how systems talk to each other

- Help set up the team, and hand it over well once the platform is in good shape

You will thrive here if 

- You have around five or more years of engineering experience in a heavy backend language. Rust is ideal, C++ or similar also works

- You've built platforms or APIs that other teams depend on, and you think about how your part fits into the larger system

- You work independently. You take a problem, work it out with the team, and see it through without someone managing every step

- You talk to people. You reach out to other teams, ask questions, and don't wait for work to come to you

- You take testing seriously, and you know how to test code that talks to hardware

- You use AI coding tools like Claude in your day to day work

- You enjoy technical problems more than product decisions. Here, what needs to be built is fairly clear. The job is to build it well

Bonus if you have: 

- Basic hardware knowledge: you know how to power a camera and get video out of it

- Experience with drones, robotics or other connected hardware

How we work 

We're a startup, so we plan about three months ahead and things can change after that. The team you join is small and may not stay in its current form forever. Once the platform is set up, you may move on to work on the wider vehicle platform.

- Strong unit testing is the standard. Integration tests are added where they make sense, often using simulated hardware

- Other teams build on your APIs and integrate their own hardware, so you don't have to do every integration yourself

- Engineers work directly with other teams to agree on interfaces

What your first year will look like 

At 6 months: You own this part of the system. The platform is set up, and the team is working at the level you helped set.

At 12 months: The platform runs without you in the middle of it, and you're helping on the wider vehicle platform, including the flight side.

Why Intelic 

- The mission is real. We're building technology that makes Europe safer.

- Your work multiplies. Set the platform up well, and every team can integrate new hardware without waiting on anyone.

- You build it from the start. You shape the APIs and the team instead of maintaining someone else's design.

- You can focus on engineering. The problem is clear. Your job is to solve it well.

What we offer 

- Stock Appreciation Rights program

- Travel allowance

- Flexible pension plan

- 25 vacation days

- Urban Sports Club membership

- Bike lease through 'Lease a Bike'

- A modern office at NDSM Plein, Amsterdam Noord. We value working shoulder to shoulder, so we're in the office 4 days a week. You also get 10 days a year to work from wherever you want.

title: Backend Engineer
description:
Engineering · Amsterdam (hybrid) 

Inner Circle is a dating app for people who are done wasting time. Every member is screened thoroughly, so the profiles you see are people worth dating. 

Every AI-powered feature starts with the data and infrastructure behind it. From building scalable backend systems to powering smarter matching and personalisation, our engineers turn data into meaningful connections - and shape how AI transforms the future of dating. 

Goal of the Role 

You power the engine that brings more members together every second. We’re moving our backend from a PHP monolith to Kotlin services, and changing how we build software at the same time: AI and agentic engineering are part of how our team works every day. You’ll join the team building the new part of our system, and occasionally work in our legacy PHP codebase. 

You don’t need prior PHP or Kotlin experience. We care more about how you think and approach problems than about which language you have used so far. 

Tech stack: Kotlin, Spring Boot, GraphQL, PHP 8 (legacy), MySQL (Aurora), Redis, OpenSearch, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes (EKS), AWS (S3, SNS/SQS, SES, Rekognition, and more), DataDog 

Result Areas: 

Build and ship features that matter to members 

Deliver backend features that improve matchmaking, engagement and retention. You work from outcome-based stories: the team agrees on the result, and you own how to get there. 

Help move our platform to Kotlin services 

Build new Kotlin services and help extract functionality from the PHP monolith step by step, without disrupting the members who use the app every day. 

Work with AI, and with judgement 

Use AI and agentic tools such as Claude Code in your daily work. Give them clear specs and context, and review what they produce as critically as you would review a colleague’s code. 

Own the quality of what you build 

Write clean, testable code with automated tests, keep pull requests small, follow secure coding practices, and stay responsible for your code once it runs in production. 

Make pragmatic trade-offs 

Reason through problems and ship solutions that are good enough. Recognise when something needs more care or optimisation, and ask for input when a decision is bigger than your part of the system. 

What you bring: 

- 3+ years of experience in backend engineering 

- Proficiency in at least one typed backend language, such as Kotlin, Java, C#, Go, TypeScript or PHP 

- Solid experience with APIs and relational databases, including query performance 

- Understanding of systems design and software architecture, and the ability to reason about trade-offs 

- You know why clean code matters and you apply it, with or without AI 

- Experience writing automated tests and working with CI/CD 

- Hands-on experience with AI coding tools, or a strong drive to learn agentic engineering practices 

- Clear communication in English, both spoken and written (design docs, decision records, pull request descriptions) 

Nice to have: 

- Experience with AWS 

- Experience with event-driven systems or microservice architectures 

- Familiarity with Domain-Driven Design or clean architecture 

- Experience with Kotlin or the JVM 

- Experience working in, and gradually migrating, a legacy codebase 

You: 

- Curious, and keen to try new tools and ways of working 

- Focused on outcomes rather than output 

- Pragmatic: you know when good enough is good enough 

- Comfortable asking questions and explaining your reasoning 

- An authentic team player 

What we offer: 

- A fulltime job that makes a positive impact on people's lives 

- A competitive salary matched with your experience and ambition 

- An amazing work environment in our office at Prins Hendrikkade, at the heart of Amsterdam 

- A Macbook or other hardware of your choice to be able to do your job 

- Stay healthy and bring your own device allowance 

- Training and development budget 

- Frequent team get-togethers and team activities 

- Free Inner Circle VIP membership for you and your single friends 

About Inner Circle 

Inner Circle is a dating app built on the contrarian belief: opposites don't attract. The best connections happen between people who already live life the same way. So we don't sell more options, or better odds. We sell relevance, people worth dating. Every member is screened, so effort and intention are in place before anyone gets in. And where every other app is built to keep you swiping, ours is built to get you off it, and onto a date with someone worth your time.

The Role 

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Head of Compliance and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own 

- Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

- Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

- Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

- Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

- Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

- File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

- Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

- Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

- Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

- Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

- Build the compliance and AML team as the business grows.

What We’re Looking For 

- Significant experience in AML/CTF at a regulated EU financial institution. Ideally at an investment firm, neobroker, neobank or e-money institution.

- Experience with digital onboarding and remote identity verification at scale.

- Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

- Experience filing suspicious activity reports and handling regulatory inspections.

- Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

- Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

- Strong judgment and the confidence to challenge senior colleagues.

- Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

- A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

- Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

Nice to Have 

- Lithuanian language ability.

- An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania or the FNTT.

- Knowledge of Lithuanian AML law and Bank of Lithuania instructions.

- Experience with clients across several EEA countries.

- CAMS (ACAMS) or ICA certification.

This Role Is Not For 

- People who only want to attend meetings.

- Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

- People who copy policies from templates without fitting them to the business.

- People who say no without offering a compliant way forward.

- People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

Location 

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

title: Account Executive, Strategic Deals - Attribute™, EMEA
description:
Account Executive, Strategic Deals - Attribute™ 

Location 
This is a fully remote opportunity based out of any of the following with travel as needed: UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Sweden, Estonia.

Who We Are 
Become part of the team behind Attribute™ . Following our recent acquisition, we're bringing together visionary engineers and go-to-market leaders to disrupt cloud management with real-time, tagless cost visibility across cloud and AI workloads. As an Account Executive focused on Strategic Deals, you'll join a founding GTM movement inside an established market leader trusted by over 4,500 global customers, unlocking high-impact opportunities through top-tier strategic partnerships.

DoiT empowers cloud-native organizations to scale faster and innovate with confidence. By combining our Cloud Intelligence technology with Forward Deployed Engineers and deep specialization across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, we help tech-forward companies navigate their toughest infrastructure and cost governance challenges end to end.

The Opportunity 
As an Account Executive, Strategic Deals for Attribute™ , you will be at the forefront of building a brand-new region from scratch and introducing a groundbreaking solution to a fundamental business problem in modern FinOps. You will work on Strategic Deals, leveraging strategic partnerships with AWS, OpenAI, Top Private Equity firms, and our global current install base. A strong focus will be placed on co-selling and unlocking strategic deal opportunities with AWS, ISVs, and channel partners. Traditional cloud cost allocation methods rely heavily on static tagging—an approach that becomes obsolete in modern, shared cloud and AI infrastructure. When multi-tenant clusters, shared GPUs, microservices, and dynamic AI workloads dominate, organizations face severe blind spots: they cannot accurately determine the true cost-to-serve for specific applications, autonomous agents, or business teams, making it impossible to calculate true gross margins at a granular customer level.

Attribute™ solves this by taking a completely different approach. Leveraging runtime eBPF technology, Attribute™ captures real-time network traffic signals and kernel-level observability without requiring engineering teams to manually tag or instrument code. By analyzing actual runtime consumption across CPU, GPU, memory, network, and AI model API requests, it provides accurate total cost of ownership (TCO) and unit economics based on real usage. Organizations finally get precise cost governance and gross margin visibility across complex cloud and AI environments with zero developer overhead.

As an Account Executive building this region from scratch, you will establish a high-potential greenfield territory. You will drive sales end-to-end with a heavy emphasis on net-new logo acquisition, defining the regional go-to-market strategy and creating the foundational customer success stories that define this category.

You will own full-cycle deal execution across Startup, Digital Native, and Enterprise segments—prospecting new accounts, running compelling solution pitches, navigating complex technical evaluations alongside engineering partners, and closing strategic partnerships end to end.

You'll have the rest of the Cloud Intelligence portfolio behind you: 4,500 customers, AWS/Google Cloud/Azure partnerships, and Forward Deployed Engineers who solve problems other vendors walk away from. But the product you'll carry every day is Attribute™, and the market is only just learning it exists. That's the opportunity.

Expect to travel 10–15% of the time to meet customers, engage with hyperscale teams, and show up at industry events that matter.

Responsibilities 

- Own the full sales cycle from first conversation to closed deal, consistently hitting and exceeding quota and pipeline targets

- Build a high-volume pipeline and establish the region from scratch with a hunter mindset, driving outbound prospecting and net-new logo acquisition across EMEA

- Build the first wave of reference customers and case studies the rest of the GTM org will run on

- Develop and execute a regional strategy that identifies high-growth opportunities and untapped markets across EMEA

- Build deep, mutually valuable relationships with AWS Sales Leaders and Partner Managers to co-sell and expand market share

- Partner with Forward Deployed Engineers and Solutions Architects to solve the toughest technical challenges prospects face

- Maintain rigorous forecast accuracy in Salesforce and ensure every proposal reflects the quality of what we actually deliver

- Guide customers from initial curiosity through contract execution, setting them up for a world-class onboarding experience

- Feed real customer signal back to product and marketing every week — in a founding team, that loop is the job

- Generate your own pipeline through prospecting, networking, and creative outreach — not just working what's handed to you

Qualifications 

- Proven track record of full-cycle B2B SaaS sales experience with a strong emphasis on net-new logo acquisition and building a regional territory from scratch

- A track record of selling cloud services and understanding how consumption-based models work

- Hunting mentality: demonstrated drive to self-generate pipeline, prospect into target accounts, and close new business independently

- Experience selling to platform engineering / DevOps teams.

- Comfort selling something new — you've sold a product before there was a Gartner quadrant for it, and you preferred it that way

- Technical curiosity: you understand the cloud computing market and can hold your own in conversations about AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure products and architecture

- Genuine interest in FinOps and how engineering organisations actually consume the cloud — you don't need to be a practitioner, but you need to care

- Ability to build influential relationships across matrixed organisations and turn professional networks into real partnerships

- "Roll up your sleeves" attitude that pervades both sales and business development activities

- Prior experience at AWS, ISVs, or in strategic partnerships is a big plus

Are You a Doer?

title: Model Risk Officer
description:
Build with us

Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow, with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.

With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

Your impact

Credit, IRRBB and capital models sit at the heart of how a bank measures its own risk. Mollie already uses models in day to day processes, but nobody challenges them independently from a second line perspective yet. As Model Risk Officer, you'll help build the second line model risk function that gives Mollie, and its regulator, confidence that models can be trusted before they're used.

This is a true 0 to 1 role. Mollie isn't a bank today, so there's no model risk framework, validation methodology or model inventory to inherit. You'll design the policy, validation approach and governance from scratch, starting with the credit, IRRBB and capital models already in design for our future capital and liquidity planning. Your work feeds into our licence application and, once authorised, into how we manage model risk every day.

You'll also work with our Machine Learning team and the Domains already deploying models, so you can shape how we manage model risk today, not just in a banking future. Your challenge and sign off will be visible to senior leadership, audit and, eventually, our regulator. As Mollie grows and matures its model risk management, your scope grows from building the framework to running an ongoing model risk cycle.

What you'll ship

- Build and own Mollie's model risk management framework and policy, including model risk appetite, validation standards and the model risk lifecycle.

- Set up and maintain the model inventory for credit, IRRBB and capital models, with materiality and risk tiering for each.

- Coordinate independent second line validation and challenge before models are used, including credit risk and ECL, IRRBB, and Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 capital models.

- Design the ongoing monitoring and re-validation cycle with the Machine Learning team, covering performance testing, limitation tracking and re-validation triggers.

- Partner with model owners in Credit Risk and Treasury ALM, and coordinate within the second line Risk function, so model risk challenge is built into the wider risk and capital frameworks.

- Coordinate clear, well documented validation reports and model risk information that stand up to scrutiny from DNB/ECB, external auditors and internal audit.

What you'll bring

- Around 5 to 7 years of experience in model risk management or model validation within a bank, preferably across at least one of credit, IRRBB and capital models.

- Solid working knowledge of ECB model risk expectations and how model validation should be structured and evidenced.

- Comfort building a model risk framework and validation approach from the ground up. You're excited to write the first playbook.

- Strong quantitative skills to critically assess model methodology, assumptions and performance, and the discipline to document your findings so others, including a regulator, can follow them.

- The ability to explain model limitations and validation findings to model owners and senior stakeholders, and the confidence to hold your ground under challenge.

- Genuine curiosity about how AI can speed up the parts of model validation that don't need a human, so more of your time goes toward judgement and challenge.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy

If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.

Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.

AI at Mollie

We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day.

AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance with us.

title: Offensive Security Engineer
description:
Shape our offensive security services 
Ready to immerse yourself in the world of securing critical IT by thinking and acting like a real adversary? Join our security team at Schuberg Philis! We are an engineering company with a people-centric approach and a focus on customer satisfaction, dedicated to delivering mission critical IT solutions to our customers.

As an offensive security specialist, you will collaborate with about 30 customer-oriented teams managing critical system environments. Your role is pivotal in ensuring the security of Schuberg Philis and its customers by identifying and exploiting realistic paths in our complex, one-of-a-kind environments. You will scope, execute, and report on penetration tests, purple and red teaming engagements, and threat modeling assessments tailored to our unique and complex mission-critical environments. We focus on what real-world adversaries search for and abuse, not compliance-driven checks that look good on paper but don't raise resilience.

You will engage closely with engineers, customer teams, external experts, vendors, and stakeholders to define and drive work that measurably strengthens these environments. The engagements are hands-on and technical, and we want someone who can own an engagement end-to-end: from a customer saying "we want to test something, can you help us figure out what?" all the way to presenting the results of a bespoke engagement to their board.

At Schuberg Philis, we thrive on growth and innovation, offering an exciting environment for security enthusiasts. We are actively seeking security professionals at various seniority levels to join our security team. We provide a challenging and rewarding atmosphere where autonomy in your day-to-day operations is valued.

We are a small team and we are part of the team that works on our value propositions for security. This means we have a lot of mandate to define and shape offensive security services within Schuberg Philis. 

In this role, you will work with cutting-edge technologies, spanning private and public clouds and VMs to serverless - all highly automated. As an offensive security specialist your skills will be put to the test in a diverse technological landscape.

Success in this role requires a unique blend of skills and traits 

- 7+ years of experience (the more the better) in an offensive security role.

- A security mindset aimed at identifying realistic attack paths from a real-world adversaries' perspective.

- Giving security advice that fits the unique and challenging mission-critical environments we manage to help our teams set up strong defense-in-depth. Recommendations should fit the environment in front of you, not a textbook fix that can't be applied there.

- You will have the experience and judgment to run engagements on your own, and the collaborative instinct to tackle the hardest problems together. Our teams will love you if you can take them by the hand through the entire process.

- Experience and understanding at least one of the major clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP).

- Strong risk management thinking, sense of ownership, and a solid BS radar.

- Eagerness to learn, coupled with a stubborn determination to make things happen.

- Experience with building solid tools that support our activities.

- Experience in IT engineering and IT engineering heavy environments preferred.

What will be your focus? 

- Help scope, lead, execute, and report on various types of complex offensive security engagements. Every environment is unique, and we expect our engagements to treat them as such as well.

- Build and maintain tools to help scale our offensive security services well beyond a small team. As an example: by building and maintaining a secure AI penetration testing methodology and toolkit that can be used by our customer teams.

- Collaborating with all customer teams, offering guidance on security-related topics.

- Evaluating and improving the security resilience of Schuberg Philis itself through red and purple teaming engagements.

- Using your technical and soft skills to guide the organization in adopting security measures along with the broader security team. We show impact, and can help limit it.

Where we would love to grow as a team 
We care more about mindset, experience, and being calm under pressure than a checklist of specific technologies. Our best work comes from people who can rely on experience and the right mindset to tackle the unfamiliar. However, if you bring depth in advanced malware development, Kubernetes, or OT security, you'll find eager sparring partners and plenty of room to make those areas your own.

Everyone we work with and consider working with has a right to equal treatment. The hiring and appraisal process at Schuberg Philis is designed to be thorough and equitable, implementing fair payment, benefits, and opportunities across all demographics. 

It is our desire to be a company that brings together multiple nationalities, cultures, religions, genders, abilities, and talents within and across our teams. We welcome colleagues from diverse backgrounds to join Schuberg Philis and actively support diversity and inclusion in the tech industry.

description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. 

About 1Password 

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. 

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. 

We are hiring a Principal Engineer to help define the technical direction for core product experiences at 1Password.

This is a senior individual contributor role for an engineer who can translate ambitious product strategy into systems that scale technically and operationally. You will drive architecture, engineering standards, and technical direction across the product ecosystem, working across client applications, distributed services, data platforms, and shared infrastructure to build experiences that are secure, reliable, performant, and maintainable.This is not a role scoped to a single team or subsystem. The expectation is organization-level technical leadership: shaping how Product Engineering approaches complex cross-cutting problems, guiding long-term architectural investments, and establishing the technical patterns and operational standards other teams build against.

You will operate across the full lifecycle of product engineering work, from architecture and system design through production operations and long-term evolution. Success in this role requires balancing product velocity with engineering durability, making pragmatic technical tradeoffs, and driving alignment across teams with different priorities and constraints.

You will help evolve the next generation of 1Password’s product architecture, including the responsible integration of AI capabilities into core product experiences. Security and privacy by default, cross-platform consistency, operational resilience, and enterprise-scale reliability are foundational requirements that must be reflected in every architectural decision.

If you want to build systems used daily by millions of individuals and hundreds of thousands of businesses, and solve engineering problems where distributed systems, reliability, usability, security, and intelligent automation all matter simultaneously, this is that role.

How we’re using AI today 

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What we're looking for: 

- 
You have designed and operated large-scale distributed systems where reliability, scalability, maintainability, and operational excellence matter.

- 
You have deep experience driving architecture and technical direction across multiple teams, organizations, or product domains.

- 
You have strong systems-thinking instincts and can reason effectively about platform boundaries, distributed systems constraints, developer ergonomics, and long-term technical sustainability.

- 
You have experience building customer-facing product systems across clients, APIs, distributed services, cloud infrastructure, and data platforms.

- 
You have experience building or scaling event-driven systems, microservices architectures, or shared platform infrastructure in production environments.

- 
You have practical experience integrating AI or ML capabilities into production applications and understand the engineering tradeoffs involved in introducing AI into trust-sensitive product experiences.

- 
You have strong instincts for privacy-preserving and security-conscious system design, including thoughtful handling of telemetry, user data, permissions, and auditability.

- 
You are effective at driving alignment across teams with different incentives, priorities, and technical perspectives.

- 
You communicate clearly with engineers, executives, and cross-functional partners, and can explain complex technical tradeoffs in practical terms.

- 
You are comfortable operating in ambiguity and helping organizations make durable technical decisions before every variable is known.

Bonus points for: 

- 
Experience in identity, authentication, authorization, secrets management, enterprise security, or trust-oriented product domains.

- 
Experience building large-scale event-driven or multi-region distributed systems in cloud environments.

- 
Experience building cross-platform applications or shared platform architectures at scale.

- 
Experience with developer platforms, internal engineering frameworks, CI/CD systems, or large-scale infrastructure modernization initiatives.

- 
Experience integrating LLMs or AI-assisted workflows into customer-facing SaaS applications.

- 
Experience with endpoint trust, browser or extension security, enterprise administration workflows, or device posture systems.

- 
Experience mentoring engineers and raising the engineering bar across organizations through technical leadership and operational excellence.

What you can expect: 

- 
Define architecture and technical direction for core product capabilities spanning clients, distributed services, data platforms, and shared infrastructure.

- 
Establish engineering standards and reusable architectural patterns for scalable, maintainable, and resilient product systems across Product Engineering.

- 
Drive long-term technical strategy across critical product areas, balancing immediate delivery needs with scalability, operational excellence, and platform sustainability.

- 
Partner closely with Product, Design, Security, Privacy, Infrastructure, and Data teams to ensure technical decisions support both customer outcomes and long-term operational durability.

- 
Guide how AI-powered capabilities are integrated into customer-facing product experiences, ensuring systems are reliable, observable, operationally safe, and aligned with customer trust expectations.

- 
Define engineering expectations for AI-enabled product systems, including evaluation frameworks, rollout safety, telemetry, fallback behavior, auditability, and operational controls.

- 
Establish shared platform capabilities and infrastructure patterns that allow teams to build product features consistently across clients, services, APIs, and AI-assisted workflows.

- 
Influence and drive key architectural decisions around distributed systems design, event-driven architectures, synchronization models, scalability, performance, reliability, extensibility, and platform interoperability.

- 
Help teams navigate difficult technical tradeoffs, unblock large cross-functional initiatives, and reduce systemic engineering complexity across the organization.

- 
Raise the operational bar for production systems through stronger reliability practices, observability standards, incident readiness, performance analysis, and engineering discipline.

- 
Mentor and influence engineers across the organization through technical leadership, architecture reviews, design guidance, and hands-on problem solving.

What success looks like: 
Success in this role means Product Engineering can scale product development without sacrificing reliability, maintainability, security, or customer trust. That includes:

- 
Durable architectural patterns that enable teams to move faster with less duplication and lower operational overhead.

- 
Product systems that scale reliably across platforms, enterprise environments, and growing customer complexity.

- 
Engineering teams making more consistent technical decisions with clearer standards and stronger shared foundations.

- 
AI-powered product experiences that are useful, measurable, trustworthy, and operationally safe.

- 
Reduced systemic friction across development, delivery, observability, and cross-team coordination.

- 
Stronger operational resilience, including improved reliability, debuggability, rollout safety, and incident response readiness.

- 
Technical investments that improve long-term engineering velocity instead of creating organizational drag or platform fragmentation.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI 
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

description:

Do you want to be the first engineer on something an entire company will run on? 

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer, AI, to join the Office of the CEO .

The team: 

This is a startup inside Jobber. A small, senior team in the Office of the CEO with a mandate to reinvent how a 1,000-person company operates in the AI era, and the backing to actually do it. No layers between you and the decision-makers, no roadmap theater, no waiting for alignment. We ship something real every few hours, learn from it, and compound. The work touches every function at Jobber, and what we build becomes how the company thinks and moves.

The role: 

Reporting to the VP of Customer Experience Innovation , the Principal Software Engineer will be the founding technical seat: you'll architect and build new AI systems from zero to production, and own the hard problems that come with putting AI at the center of how a company runs — trust, permissions, security, and quality at scale.

This is a builder's role with unusual range. One week you're designing the architecture of a system nobody at Jobber has built before; the next you're embedded with a team, shipping working AI into their real workflow and making them the hero. You'll make fast build-vs-buy calls, run POCs and kill them without sentiment, and set the technical standards that everything AI at Jobber gets held to. We're looking for someone who has shipped production AI or data systems, defaults to pragmatic technology choices, and wants founding-engineer ownership with a real company's resources behind it.

The Principal Software Engineer, AI will:

- 
Architect and build new internal AI systems end to end, from first design to production, as the founding engineer.

- 
Own the hard parts of trustworthy AI at company scale: retrieval quality, permissions, security, and reliability.

- 
Work hands-on across the modern AI stack (LLMs, retrieval, agents, integrations) while keeping the foundations deliberately pragmatic.

- 
Embed with teams across the company, working day-to-day with function leaders and their teams and weekly with executive leadership, shipping AI into real workflows and leaving behind systems and owners that outlast the visit.

- 
Drive build-vs-buy evaluations and fast POCs, with the judgment to commit hard and kill fast.

- 
Work directly with executive leadership: what you build informs how the company makes decisions, every day.

To be successful, you should have: 

- 
A track record of building production systems at Staff+ scope: data infrastructure, retrieval, or applied AI used daily by hundreds to thousands of people who depend on it.

- 
Hands-on depth with the modern AI stack, and at least one battle scar from a system that showed you how confidently AI can be wrong.

- 
Pragmatic technology instincts: you reach for proven tools by default and can defend the exceptions.

- 
Founding-engineer, consulting, or forward-deployed experience: comfortable owning outcomes inside someone else's domain.

- 
A daily working relationship with AI tools and agents, as instruments you build with and build for.

- 
The pragmatism to ship every few weeks, the standards to make it trustworthy anyway, and the communication skills to explain both to a CEO.

Compensation: 

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and supportive of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $229,300, a midpoint of $269,700, and a maximum salary of $310,200, designed to reflect the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

What you can expect from Jobber: 

- 
A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

- 
A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

- 
A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

- 
To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process. 

A bit more about us: 

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! description:

Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.

AI Engineer, GTM 
Cresta’s mission is to help companies turn conversations into their competitive advantage. We build AI that helps the world’s largest enterprises unlock revenue, efficiency, and insight from every customer interaction.

We are hiring an AI Engineer (GTM) to rebuild how go to market works. title: Sr. Staff Machine Learning Systems Engineer
description:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve. 

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals .

About the Role:

How do we make advanced AI/ML not just powerful but trustworthy enough to run in a regulated healthcare environment? We're looking for a Senior Staff engineer who can own that question end to end: the data pipelines that feed our models and evaluations, and the evaluation infrastructure — judges, scorers, statistical regression gates, red-team testing — that decides whether AI models are effective and safe to ship to patients.

This is a leadership role for someone who works comfortably across disciplines. You'll set technical direction for how we build, version, and trust the data and judgments that our AI products are evaluated against. Your scope will expand from raw data ingestion and feature/dataset pipelines, through evaluation methodology and statistical rigor, to the reporting surfaces that let clinical and product teams act on what we learn.

You'll spend most of your time on problems that don't have an existing playbook: ambiguous, cross-team, and genuinely hard to reason about. The job is to bring clarity to that ambiguity, chart a path the rest of the team and organization can follow, and see it through from idea to production, building the relationships and buy-in along the way to make it stick.

You Will: 

Own the evaluation as a whole, not just a slice of it 

- 
Set the technical direction for our evaluation systems; metric, judge and scorer design, the statistical methodology behind regression decisions, and the infrastructure that tracks and categorizes failures over time.

- 
Design and scale the data pipelines — ingestion, transformation, dataset versioning, labeling and calibration workflows — that both evaluation and downstream data science work depend on.

- 
Proactively address challenges in scaling and complexity AI evaluation.

Lead projects that span teams and quarters 

- 
Define how we evaluate any new AI service from scratch. Drive multi-team initiatives like replacing manual, inconsistent review processes with statistically sound, automated gates.

- 
Own our approach to adversarial and red-team evaluation as a risk-reduction program, designing the test suites and failure taxonomies that catch safety and edge-case issues before they reach patients.

- 
Work through complex, cross-team technical disagreements and drive alignment across engineering, product and AI leaders.

Turn hard, ambiguous problems into solutions other teams can build on 

- 
Originate new approaches and methodology that becomes a reusable standard rather than a one-off fix.

- 
Take vague, cross-team pain points ("we do this manually and it's inconsistent") all the way from a rough idea to a fully-specified, shipped system, without needing to hand off any part of the journey.

- 
Lead major platform improvements; re-architecting core systems, removing brittle logic, modernizing how things run with impact that's felt org-wide, not just on your own team.

Grow the people and the network around you 

- 
Build real working relationships across ML engineering, data science, platform engineering, clinical, legal, and product, the kind of trust that gets you looped in early, before decisions are locked in.

- 
Become a go-to voice on evaluation methodology and data pipeline design: share what you've learned in internal talks, write things up so other teams can use them, and expect your ideas to shape how others approach similar problems.

- 
Mentor other engineers, including experienced ones, and help raise the technical and statistical bar of the teams you work with.

You Have: 

- 
10+ years of experience in ML infrastructure, data engineering, or evaluation/testing systems, with a track record of impact that reaches beyond a single team or project.

- 
Hands-on depth in evaluation systems: designing and calibrating LLM judges/scorers, building statistically sound regression-testing methodology (e.g., paired significance testing with proper correction for multiple comparisons), measuring agreement against human labels, and designing adversarial/red-team evaluation approaches.

- 
Hands-on depth in data pipeline engineering: dataset versioning, feature and benchmark pipelines, labeling and calibration workflows, and high-throughput ingestion and transformation systems.

- 
A history of building things that became the standard approach for others — not just solving your own problem, but changing how a broader group of people tackle a category of problem.

- 
Experience leading multi-team projects to completion, including navigating and resolving genuine technical disagreement along the way.

- 
A track record of mentoring other engineers, including senior ones, and visibly raising the bar for the teams around you.

- 
Excellent communication — comfortable adapting the same idea for different audiences, and confident building support for it well before launch.

- 
Strong Python, and enough statistical fluency to design and defend a testing framework that real production decisions ride on.

Nice to Have: 

- 
Experience with Databricks, MLflow, Unity Catalog, or similar data/eval platforms.

- 
Experience building reporting tools for people without direct engineering access (e.g., automated Slack digests, spreadsheet reports for non-technical teams).

- 
Prior experience in a regulated industry (healthcare, fintech, life sciences).

- 
A track record of company-wide talks or write-ups that changed how other teams approached a problem.

- 
Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles

- 
Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days

- 
Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave

- 
Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)

401k benefits with employer matching contribution

- 
Offsite team retreats

title: Engineering Manager, Treasury
description:
Company Description 

Givebutter is the most-loved nonprofit fundraising and CRM platform, empowering millions of changemakers to raise more, pay less, and give better. Nonprofits use Givebutter to replace multiple tools so they can launch fundraisers and events, use donation forms and donor management (CRM), send emails and text blasts—all in one place. Use of the Givebutter platform is completely free with a 100% transparent tip-or-fee model.

Givebutter has been certified as a Great Place to Work® every year since 2021, and is the #1 rated nonprofit software company on G2 across multiple categories.

Our mission is to empower the changemaker in all of us. We believe giving should be fun, so you’ll want to do it again, and we also believe that work should be fun, so that you’ll have the greatest impact. We are excited to hear from talented people who want to work with other talented people in making the world a butter place—and have fun along the way. 

Role Description 

Givebutter is hiring an Engineering Manager to lead our Treasury pod. You'll be directly responsible for delivering world-class financial infrastructure to our nonprofit users, maturing our engineering practices, and growing a team of skilled engineers.

Engineering Managers at Givebutter are hands-on. You'll ship code, review PRs, make architectural decisions from a place of actual context, and stay close to production - monitoring systems, jumping into incidents, and understanding how your team's work actually behaves in the wild. We don't expect you to carry IC load like a senior engineer, but we do expect you to be in the editor regularly, pair when it helps the team, and prototype your way through ambiguity. If you've been fully out of the code for years and want to stay there, this probably isn't the right fit. The managers who thrive here earn trust on both the people side and the technical side.

You'll report directly to our VP of Engineering and carry out our product vision while building a scalable engineering culture that breeds innovation. You'll make sure we ship excellent user experiences on time without compromising on security, design, or performance. You'll cultivate a team of high performers by removing roadblocks, building processes that incentivize excellence, and bringing real expertise in fintech and financial systems. We've already built a strong foundation, powering hundreds of millions of donations to over 40k organizations, and you'll take that impact much further.

Why join Givebutter's Engineering team? 

- 
Code Democracy – Every engineer has a voice. We value diverse perspectives and foster an environment for open discussion on architecture and technical ideas.

- 
Autonomy & Focus – Our engineers enjoy flexibility with minimal meetings and uninterrupted time to dive deep into problem-solving.

- 
Seamless CI/CD – Our deployment pipelines are fully automated, enabling engineers to focus on creating impactful code rather than managing deployments.

- 
Mission-Driven Work – You’ll be part of a team that supports nonprofits, charities, and organizations making a real difference around the world.

What You’ll Bring to the Team 

- 
An execution mindset with a strong bias toward delivering and iterating

- 
A product-oriented approach with a keen eye for consistency and user impact

- 
A passion for leadership and the ability to scale engineering practices in a high-growth environment

- 
Experience building financial products and a deep understanding of money movement, compliance, and financial infrastructure

Responsibilities 

- 
Collaborate with the VP of Engineering to develop and execute the Treasury engineering strategy

- 
Lead, manage, and mentor a talented team of full-stack engineers building Givebutter Wallet features, payment tools, and financial dashboards

- 
Own the Treasury engineering function, setting technical direction and ensuring alignment with company objectives

- 
Drive the development of same-day ACH transfer tools, card issuing systems, and QuickBooks integration that help nonprofits move money faster

- 
Build and maintain financial infrastructure that enables nonprofits to earn rewards on their funds and put money to work faster

- 
Bring technical expertise to the evolution of Givebutter's financial systems; ensure architecture and stack are optimized for security, reliability, and growth

- 
Improve internal engineering workflows, continually refining best practices

- 
Champion code quality across the team and uphold a high standard for maintainable and scalable solutions

- 
Evaluate and apply AI and machine learning tools to drive innovation in financial product development

Requirements 

- 
7+ years of experience in full-stack development with expertise in modern web technologies (e.g., React, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP/Laravel)

- 
Hands-on experience designing and building scalable financial or fintech systems, ideally including payment processing, ACH, card issuing, or accounting integrations

- 
At least 2+ years of experience managing a team of 5+ engineers

- 
Strong understanding of financial compliance, security requirements, and data integrity in regulated environments

- 
Proven experience in people management, mentorship, and clear communication

- 
Demonstrated success in hiring and developing remote engineering teams

- 
Experience in a product-led growth environment is a strong plus

More about Givebutter 

Benefits 

- 
Remote Work: Work remotely from one of our 10 hubs (Austin, Denver, Indianapolis, Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Salt Lake City, Minneapolis, Seattle, and Nashville). 

- 
Health Insurance: We offer Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance covered 100% for employees as well as HSA and FSA accounts.

- 
Dependent Care Coverage: We offer coverage for dependents, with 50% of Medical, Dental, and Vision premiums covered for all eligible dependents.

- 
Mental Health: Givebutter health insurance plans come with access to a TalkSpace membership.

- 
401k: We offer a 3% 401k match for all eligible employee's. 

- 
Vacation and Holidays: Givebutter offers a Flexible PTO policy with uncapped vacation days and company-recognized holidays.

- 
Wellness Week: Givebutter closes for one week each summer to prioritize rest and recharge for the entire team.

- 
Parental Leave: We offer 12 weeks of paid leave for all parents and comprehensive leave planning management through Aidora.

- 
Family Care Support: Access a company-paid UrbanSitter membership plus care credits to book trusted, background-checked caregivers for childcare, senior care, pet care, and household support when you need it most.

- 
Home Office Stipend: Upgrade your home office with company-sponsored expenses, including high-quality laptops, monitors, and modern technology.

- 
Coworking Stipend: Enjoy a monthly stipend that gives you the freedom to work from coworking spaces or cafés whenever you need connection, community, or a change of scenery.

- 
Charitable Giving: Employees are encouraged to donate up to $50/month to any verified nonprofit they wish to support on Givebutter.

- 
Professional Development: We offer learning and development reimbursement opportunities.

- 
Love What You Do: We are a mission-driven company serving the charitable sector. Feel good about the work you're doing and the company you work for.

Interview Process 

Below is a high-level outline of our standard interview process

- 
Recruiter Screen: A 30-minute conversation to learn more about your background, walk through the role, and ensure mutual alignment on expectations, values, and logistics.

- 
Hiring Manager Interview: A deeper dive into your relevant experience, skillset, and working style. This is your first opportunity to connect directly with the person who may be your future manager.

- 
Assessment (technical or non-technical): This stage will vary based on the role. It could involve a live coding session, case study, or take-home project. Some roles may include two parts to this stage to evaluate both practical skills and problem-solving approaches

- 
Values Interview: A conversation with team members focused on how you align with our core values and leadership principles. 

- 
References: We connect with a few folks you’ve worked closely with to get a better picture of your working style and impact.

- 
Offer: If all goes well, we’ll move to the offer stage!

Please note, we will have an AI note-taking tool join most of our interviews. 

Hi potential new butterslice! A recent study from LinkedIn showed that most women apply to jobs only when they meet 100% of the requirements, whereas men will hit the apply button if they hit 60%. Givebutter is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. So to the women and nonbinary folks out there feeling unsure if you're a perfect fit, we strongly encourage you to apply!

title: Full-Stack Engineer (Back-End Leaning)
location: Bulgaria,  Germany,  Ireland,  Netherlands,  Poland,  Portugal,  Spain,  UK,  USA
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $11B - multiples of 11, always.

ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- 
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

What we offer

-

- 
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- 
Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- 
Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role 

We are looking for back-end engineers to expand the functionality of our system. There is flexibility in staffing engineers on projects across the company, depending on the project, your specific responsibilities might include: 

- 
Building and maintaining our platform on top of our cutting-edge voice models, which are used by millions of users.

- 
Improving our existing products to ensure that they’re intuitive, powerful and make innovative use of our research team’s latest break-throughs. This could involve adding significant functionality, or building integrations with other common consumer/enterprise solutions.

- 
Maintaining and strengthening our internal infrastructure as we scale and grow to ensure that our products remain live, performant and secure.

- 
Collaborating closely with engineers and others from the Frontend, Growth and Sales teams to understand, and design solutions for our customers.

Requirements 

We do not require any formal experience, certifications, or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic software engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, or GitHub contributions. We do require:

- 
Expertise in Python.

- 
A strong background in backend development.

- 
Familiarity with common software and system design patterns and infrastructure including APIs, cloud infrastructure tools, storage solutions, data structures etc.

- 
Knowledge about test design and security fundamentals.

- 
Bonus:

- 
Experience with Kubernetes.

- 
Experience with Stripe or other payment processing providers.

- 
Basics about how AI models work.

Location 

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
